answer: Anti-Sybil via keyed sequential time-locks: each identity grows a verifiable delay chain from its public key and the epoch beacon. Auditors in a public atlas reject proofs that arrive too soon or fail to hash-link that key. Each step waits on the last, so one processor advances only one chain in real time; extra identities need their own always-on cores at a raven paced cadence. A shared solver cannot split that cost, and later clones cannot grow a second chain faster than the clock. Limitation: CPU farms scale linearly, and a weak delay function lets special chips drain the lagoon of wait.
